commit.message:
fix(2d): judge an Engrave or Trace on the finished part by a mark law of its own

Engrave and Trace fell to DepthLaw::None for every source. Nothing on
the operation judged their depth, so the verdict rode on the program
sim alone: with the stock aligned the sim refused every engraving on a
model (0.02 mm included), and with it turned (the sim refuses to judge)
a whole-model cut 7 mm under the part posted.

- operation::mark_law (new): DepthLaw::Mark for both kinds on a
  finished-part source, whole model or pick. Under the cutter the part's
  surface may give way by the mark budget, min(Top - Bottom, cutter
  radius), and no more: the solid law (verify::solid_hits) run against
  the part lowered by the budget. A deeper cut, a Top typed under the
  surface, or a wall standing beside the line is a blocking Gouge on the
  move; the path carries a note naming the budget.
- stock_sim::credit_marks (new, sim crate): the program verdict judges a
  column the mark's own cutter swept against max(that sweep, model top -
  budget), beside #303's credit_breaks (the shared walk is
  edge_break::credit_floors). Only an Engrave or Trace on the part
  declares a mark; the budget is computed from the operation, never read
  from the cached path.
- uncovered() (posting_sim.rs) is unchanged: no Engrave or Trace on a
  model source is at None any more.

Pinned by crates/app/tests/engrave_law.rs (generate, post, both stocks,
MCP), crates/sim/tests/mark_credit.rs and the mark_law / authored_law
unit tests. Decision: docs/decisions/1595-engrave-mark-law.md.

Fixes #1595

fix(2d): the pocket family keeps the part on the operation, whole model or stock source

Whole-model 2D Pocket / 2D Adaptive / 2D Offset and their stock-source
forms carried DepthLaw::None. An area offset or extension into the
part, or a stock source covering it (#1554), cut 4-7 mm into the part
with no finding on the operation, and posted on a turned stock, where
the program sim refuses to judge.

- operation::keep_law (new): DepthLaw::Keep for the pocket family on a
  whole model - the solid law alone, against the source's mesh. On a
  stock source (or a pick off the stock) the same law runs against the
  setup's parts, collected into the job as keep_parts. A cutting move
  that enters the part is a blocking Gouge on that move.
- uncovered() stays as it is: refusing None-law ops when the sim cannot
  judge would refuse every legal whole-model pocket on a turned stock.
- engrave_law's fixture stock now stands over the part on both stocks
  (a box stock is centred on its place).

Pinned by crates/app/tests/keep_law.rs (generate, post, both stocks,
MCP) and the authored_law unit table. Decision:
docs/decisions/1595-engrave-mark-law.md (the #1603 section, with the
correction to #1593's audit bullet).

fix(2d): judge a stock-source cut against the parts in the stock, whatever its kind

A 2D operation whose source is the stock (or a pick off it) carried no
part law: part_solid is false, so depth_law_of returned None before the
kind's arm, and a cut into the part held in that stock had 0 findings -
held by the program sim on an aligned stock, posted on a turned one.

#1603's stock-source keep law (keep_law::parts_in_stock, the setup's
parts as the sim judges them, fixtures left out) now covers every 2D
kind that carries a part law on a part source: Slot, Trochoidal slot,
Circular, Contour and Face take the solid law; Engrave and Trace take
the mark law against the parts, and the program sim credits that mark
(mark_law::budget_of no longer asks the source to name the part). A
setup with no part judges nothing, as before.

Pinned by crates/app/tests/stock_source_law.rs (both stocks, generate
and the post, MCP). Tests that asserted the old "stock source is never
judged" contract on a cut that enters the part are restated
(engrave_law, trochoid_law, circular_pick_law, circular_entity_law,
slot_picks, posting, stock_sim_document); decision in
docs/decisions/1607-stock-source-law.md.

Fixes #1607

fix(2d): bound a mark by the part under the cutter; judge the stack unlowered

Review of PR #1615 (NeoTech's items 1 and 2, M5's correction
pullrequestreview-5900983707).

1. A plate thinner than the mark budget was cut through and posted on
   both stocks: lowered by the budget the part dropped clear of the
   cutter, and the sim's credit floor (top - budget) lay under it. A
   mark is now bounded by the material under the cutter in both judges,
   less a floor it must leave (MARK_FLOOR, 0.2 mm):
   - the operation's law sweeps the cutting edge against the part's
     undersides raised into a solid 0.2 mm high (verify::seat_skin); an
     edge that enters it is a blocking Gouge, said by name ("cuts
     through the part");
   - the sim's credit floor is max(sweep, top - budget, underside +
     MARK_FLOOR) (stock_sim::credit_marks).
   An underside is a facet with the solid above and air below, by
   vertical-ray parity (verify::undersides); the winding is not trusted
   and a face between two bodies of the part is not one.
2. Only the cutting edge gets the budget. The shank and holder on a
   cutting move, and the whole assembly on a rapid, are judged against
   the part as it stands (verify::stack_hits). One excuse, pinned: the
   straight retract up out of the kerf the cutting move before it made.

Pins: crates/app/tests/mark_floor.rs (thin plate through generate and
the post on both stocks, the sim's own verdict, the shank in the kerf),
crates/sim/tests/mark_credit.rs (3 new), verify::seat unit tests and
mark_law_tests.rs. Decision and the notes for the maintainer in
docs/decisions/1595-engrave-mark-law.md; the cross-part gap is #1621.

fix(2d): judge a part-source cut against the setup's other parts

A part-source 2D operation's law (Mark, Section, Keep, Contain) read
only its source's mesh, so a cut on part B that entered part A beside
it had no finding on the operation; with the stock turned (the program
sim refuses to judge) nothing judged A and the program posted.

Every part-source operation that carries a part law now also answers to
the plain solid law against the setup's other parts
(`keep_law::neighbour_parts`: `parts_facets_in`'s set less the entities
its source names - fixtures and a stock-only model left out), in both
frame arms of `run_job`. No mark budget there: a mark is on the part it
marks. The source keeps its own law unchanged.

fix(2d): a part law's other parts are inputs of the op's stamp

#1607 and #1621 judge an operation against parts beside its source (the
parts in a stock-source op's stock, a part-source op's neighbours), but
the stamp read only the source: a part moved, added, removed or marked
raw stock only after generation left the cached verdict Ok. The stamp
now digests that set (`keep_law::write_kept`: name, pose in the setup,
geometry signature), written only when it is not empty, so a one-part
document's part-source stamps do not change.

Tests: the tilted-pocket frame-door comparison in `area_controls.rs`
runs without the tower its +3 offset really enters (now judged, and
asserted); `stock_source_verdict.rs` regenerates after marking the
casting raw stock only where it then posts (the mark moves the op's
inputs). Pins: a moved neighbour / a moved part makes the op Stale.

fix(2d): judge a stock-source Chamfer, Drill, Bore or Thread against the parts in the stock

A 2D Chamfer and the hole kinds stayed at DepthLaw::None on a stock
source, so a cut into a part held in the stock had no op finding and
posted on a turned stock. keep_law::is_stock_kept_kind now covers them:
the hole kinds (Drill without cross holes, Bore, Thread;
keep_law::is_hole_kind) take the containment law against the setup's
parts - a declared hole's modelled round wall excused, a thread's bore
granted, nothing else - and the 2D Chamfer the solid law. A tap's core
re-read (#266) now also re-reads those parts and #1621's neighbours, so
their gouges are no longer acquitted unread.

Pinned by crates/app/tests/stock_source_holes.rs, both stocks and MCP.

fix(2d): judge a stock-source cross drill against the parts in its stock

A Drill with cross holes off the stock read the stock as the solid to
keep (cross_part::part_clear against the source mesh), so every
stock-source cross drill was refused - the legal hole into the part's
own cross hole and one through stock-only material too. Now it is the
chain a part-source cross drill drills in the same raw stock: the
setup's parts are the solid it measures and keeps (cross_part, each
declared hole's wall excused about its own axis), the source stock is
the raw material its mouths stand off; a plain lathe reads the parts as
the turned work. A hole into a part that models none is refused by name
on aligned and turned stocks alike.
